description:
The average elevation of the Tibetan Plateau exceeds 13,000 feet—higher than most mountain peaks in Europe.
It is one of the harshest natural environments on Earth. 
Yet for thousands of years, one of the world's most remarkable civilizations has flourished here. 
Its people learned to survive in conditions that seem impossible for human life.
